claim: A live-measured fleet of 3 NVIDIA T4 GPUs reserved 24/7 for single-tenant agent workloads cost $1,576/month and ran only a 23.5% GPU duty cycle, meaning ~$1,200/month (about 77%) was idle GPU spend.
stance_target: idle agent compute is the dominant and quantifiable cost line in fleet-scale agent deployments
scope_conditions: single-tenant deployment (model weights loaded inside the agent container, no shared inference server); GKE cluster, 3x NVIDIA T4 on n1-standard-8 nodes
quoted_support: ScaleOps put the GPU cost at $1,576/month, about $525 per node... GPU duty cycle was 23.5%... about $1,200 of the $1,576 monthly GPU spend was idle.

claim: CPU-based Horizontal Pod Autoscaling is structurally blind to GPU-bound agent workload bursts and will incorrectly scale the fleet down to minimum replicas while GPU is saturated and tasks queue up.
stance_target: naive autoscaling signals fail for agent fleets; auto-kill/scale logic must use agent-native signals (queue depth, GPU utilization), not CPU
scope_conditions: Kubernetes HPA default behavior, CPU target 50%, GPU-bound bursty workload
quoted_support: During bursts the GPU hit 100% while CPU peaked at 25%, never crossing the 50% target. The controller scaled the resident workloads down to a single replica because CPU looked idle... the task queue backed up to 7 to 10 items.

claim: Reactive queue-depth-based autoscaling (KEDA) with a warm floor only achieved a 28% reduction in average running GPUs under continuous bursty load, because burst arrival intervals (~6 min) were shorter than the default 5-minute scale-down stabilization window.
stance_target: limits of reactive (non-predictive) auto-scale-down for agent fleets
scope_conditions: KEDA ScaledObject, minReplicaCount=1, Prometheus queue-depth trigger, bursts every ~6 minutes
quoted_support: warm-mode scaling (minReplicaCount: 1) averaged 2.17 GPUs over an hour, only about a 28% reduction versus the fixed three... The big drop to one replica only happened during a genuine idle gap.
numbers: 38% utilization after denser packing vs 22% before

claim: Scaling GPU-backed agent workloads to zero avoids all idle billing but incurs a measured cold start of approximately 3.2 minutes (49 seconds node provisioning + 143 seconds scheduling/image-pull/weight-loading).
stance_target: cost of aggressive auto-kill / scale-to-zero policies on agent fleets
scope_conditions: GKE, single-tenant GPU workload, cold node + cold pod
quoted_support: we measured ~3.2 minutes for the first request after idle — 49 seconds to provision a node plus 143 seconds for pod scheduling, image pull, and loading weights into VRAM.

claim: GPU memory rightsizing from a framework-default 15GiB reservation to a measured-consumption 3.06GiB allowed roughly 5 small agent/model workloads to co-reside on a single 16GB T4 instead of 1, reclaiming about $300/month on that workload alone.
stance_target: fractional GPU sharing is a quantifiable lever for fleet-scale cost reduction distinct from replica scaling
scope_conditions: single-tenant deployment (model loaded in agent container, no pre-allocated KV cache); not applicable to tuned vLLM/Triton serving tiers where VRAM headroom is real KV cache
quoted_support: ScaleOps rightsized the per-replica GPU memory request from 15 GiB to 3.06 GiB... about five co-reside on one accelerator instead of one... It reclaims about $300/month on this single workload.

claim: Container CPU and memory requests for agent pods are typically over-padded defensively (to survive OOM failures) and can be safely rightsized in place without restarts, recovering the large majority of the padding.
stance_target: non-GPU resource rightsizing is a safe, zero-disruption cost lever for agent fleets
scope_conditions: Kubernetes in-place pod resize, agent-tier (CPU-only) pods in a split deployment
quoted_support: CPU Request 4 -> 1117m (~72% cut); Memory Request 24 GiB -> ~282 MiB (~99% cut)... the fleet converged within minutes, with zero restarts and no maintenance window.

claim: Idle GPU cost as a share of fleet spend is not a fixed ratio and depends on how many separate GPU deployments a stack runs and the duty cycle of each; a shared inference tier serving many agents via continuous batching runs a materially higher duty cycle than single-tenant deployments and may make always-on economically correct.
stance_target: a single universal 'idle cost percentage' figure can be applied across all agent fleet architectures
scope_conditions: general to any Kubernetes-hosted agent/inference architecture
quoted_support: A shared inference tier fronting many agents aggregates their bursts and runs a higher duty cycle, so read the idle share per deployment and sum it across the fleet rather than assuming 77% everywhere.
